author: Hodgson, 1833
summary: 사막, 반사막, 스텝 지대, 대초원처럼 건조한 곳을 좋아하는 수리다. 갓 죽은 고기는 종류를 가리지 않고 먹으며, 설치류와 토끼만 한 작은 포유류, 메추라기만 한 새를 사냥하고 다른 동물의 먹이를 훔치기도 한다. 나무 위에 나뭇가지로 지은 둥지에 알을 1~3개 낳고, 과시할 때를 빼면 조용하며 울음소리는 까마귀와 비슷하다. 루마니아 동부, 러시아 남부, 중앙아시아, 몽골 등지에서 번식하며, 유럽·중앙아시아 번식 집단은 아프리카에서, 동부 번식 집단은 인도에서 겨울을 난다.
young: 어린새는 어른새와 조금 다르며, 어른새와 마찬가지로 몸 색이 다양하다.

similar.how: 초원수리가 더 크고 색이 어두우며, 목이 가냘프다.

art.subject: Steppe Eagle (Aquila nipalensis), adult in winter: plumage almost uniformly dark brown on the head, body and wing coverts, often with a small rusty-buff patch on the nape; flight feathers and tail darker blackish-brown with fine grey barring; thighs fully feathered as brown trousers down to the toes; bill dark grey with a black tip; yellow cere and a long yellow gape line that runs back under the eye to its rear edge; dark brown eye; feet yellow.
art.pose: perched on top of a low tree in open dry grassland
art.scene: Korean winter: open farmland and low dry hills with a lone bare tree under a wide sky; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a bare tree: dark brown head, body and wing coverts, blackish-brown flight feathers and tail, feathered brown legs, heavy dark bill with a yellow cere and a long yellow gape reaching the rear of the eye
adult, in flight seen from below: long broad wings with fingered tips, dark brown coverts, grey finely barred flight feathers with a broad dark trailing edge, blackish-brown rounded tail
art.build: Very large, heavy eagle, 62–74cm, a little smaller than a Golden Eagle and much smaller than a Cinereous Vulture; big-headed with a heavy hooked bill shorter than the head. Legs feathered to the toes; feet yellow. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. Tail medium length, rounded. In flight long, broad, parallel-edged wings with long fingered primaries, held flat or slightly drooped at the hand; the adult underwing shows grey, finely barred flight feathers with a broad dark trailing edge.
avoid: Do not paint a golden-tawny crown and nape or a white tail base; those are Golden Eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) features.
Do not paint white shoulder patches or a pale golden crown (Eastern Imperial Eagle).
Do not paint a white tail or bare yellow legs as on sea eagles; the legs are fully feathered.
Do not paint a short gape ending in front of the eye; it extends back to the rear of the eye.
